problem:
For the sets $X={k,m,n}$ and $Z=X\times X,$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- ${k}^{2}\in Z$
- $(k,n,m)\in Z$
- $(m,n)\in Z$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $X\times X$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $X$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $X.$

In this case, the schematic for ${X}^{2}=X\times X$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040355/assets/e7c24108e0d9f5e2e7edbfbe90cdf7318bc247aa73a4c9c72dc61449c7b4da94.png)

Hence, the set $Z=X\times X$ is given by

$$
Z={(k,k),(k,m),(k,n),(m,k),(m,m),(m,n),(n,k),(n,m),(n,n)}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
